statement: Of the $900$ runners in a city race, $40\%$ are in the under-30 age group. Of the runners in the under-30 age group, $15\%$ finished the race in less than $25$ minutes. How many runners in the under-30 age group finished in less than $25$ minutes?

choices.misconception: I took 15% of all 900 runners, but the 15% applies only to the runners in the under-30 group.
I found the number of under-30 runners, 360, and forgot to take 15% of them.
I added 40% and 15% to get 55% and took 55% of 900, but the second percent is a percent of a smaller group.

hints: The $15\%$ is a percent of which group?
First find how many runners are under 30, then take $15\%$ of that number.
There are $0.40 \times 900 = 360$ runners under 30. Find $15\%$ of $360$.

solutions.reliable: Under-30 runners: $0.40 \times 900 = 360$. Of these, $15\%$ finished in less than $25$ minutes: $0.15 \times 360 = 54$ runners.
solutions.elegant: A percent of a percent multiplies: $0.40 \times 0.15 = 0.06$, so $6\%$ of all $900$ runners, which is $54$, are under 30 and finished in less than $25$ minutes.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
